...meantime, you at least keep your Altcoin exposure by holding $ETH, or whatever other asset you traded your $DOGE for. And in cash terms, you are £10k better off. 
(7/10)

Now what if you still want to hold $DOGE? You can buy it back, but you will need to wait 30 days. In the UK there is ‘bed and breakfast rules’ which prevent you selling an asset to realise a tax loss before buying straight back...
(6/10)

Remember, Crypto-to-Crypto (c2c) trades are taxable. This means you can claim a loss on c2c trades to offset your gains. 

So you trade $DOGE for $ETH. You've now locked in a loss of £50k which can be offset against the $BTC gain of £50k. Your CGT liability is now ZERO!
(5/10)

EXAMPLE: 
Let’s say you have $BTC and $DOGE.

You made gains in $BTC and wish to sell (Bought £100k, today’s value = £150k > your taxable gain is £50k)

You also made losses in $DOGE (Bought £100k, today’s value = £50k > your loss is £50k). But you don’t want to sell...
(3/10)

Example - you bought £1k worth of $DOGE.  It moons and is now worth £100k. You sell this for $SHIBA. This is a disposal and you have triggered a capital gain of £99k and a tax bill of £19.8k. 

So you now have £100k of $SHIBA and a £19.8k tax bill. BUT...

9/11
